answer: Phantom Identity Pricing. Each agent identity must attach a meaningful nectar deposit to a distinct long-lived task, and only identities that sustain that task can join a coordination river for shared work. A sparrow-level reputation score accrues slowly through verified task tenure, and agents with low scores must pay higher coordination costs for every additional identity. Attacking the system requires funding and sustaining many parallel tasks over time, paying real resource costs per identity before coordination rights unlock.
